title: Find and Group Duplicate Records in Table
code:
SELECT email, COUNT(*)
FROM users
GROUP BY email
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY count DESC;
explanation: Aggregates rows sharing the same value and filters out unique items using HAVING COUNT(*) > 1, isolating duplicate entries before applying deduplication scripts.
caveat: WHERE filters rows before grouping occurs, while HAVING filters aggregated group results after grouping.

variations.label: List full rows using window function
variations.code: SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY email ORDER BY id) as rn FROM users;

variations.label: Delete duplicates keeping lowest id
variations.code: DELETE FROM users WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT MIN(id) FROM users GROUP BY email);
